name: co-VC dimension
definition: For a binary class $\mathcal H\subseteq2^{\mathcal X}$, the **coVC number** $\mathrm{coVC}(\mathcal H)$ is the supremum of $|S|$ over finite sets $S\subseteq\mathcal X$ for which some $T\subseteq S$ satisfies $$T\notin\mathcal H_{|S}\quad\text{and}\quad T\mathbin{\triangle}\{x\}\in\mathcal H_{|S}\quad\text{for every }x\in S.$$ Such a configuration is a hollow star. The value is zero if there is no such configuration, and $+\infty$ if the sizes are unbounded. On a finite domain the supremum is a maximum whenever a hollow star exists. In particular, a full cube has value zero, whereas a one-concept class on a nonempty domain has value one.
description: The maximum dimension of a hollow star in a coordinate projection. It is also called the hollow star number, dual Helly number, or consistency dimension (up to the conventional shift used for Helly numbers).
graph_summary: Largest projected hollow star: an unrealizable labeling whose every one-coordinate flip is realizable. Also called hollow star number/co-VC dimension.
comments: On a finite domain this is also called the **consistency dimension**: the least $k$ such that every labeling outside the class has a labeled restriction of size at most $k$ inconsistent with the class. For intersection-closed or extremal classes (hence maximum classes), $\mathrm{coVC}\leq\mathrm{VC}+1$, without an exception at $\mathrm{VC}=|\mathcal X|-1$. Infinite-domain analogues require an explicit finite-sample/supremum and compactness convention; no equivalence for arbitrary infinite inconsistent samples is asserted by this finite-support definition. The conditioning evidence below concerns finite-coordinate conditioning, as automatically holds on a finite domain.
origin_references: Introduced as co-VC dimension in \cite{kane2019communication}; the equivalent dual Helly number and hollow-star formulation are developed in \cite{bousquet2020proper}. The consistency-dimension terminology appears in \cite{hegedHus1995generalized}.

monotonic.proof: For $n\ge3$, the full cube $\{0,1\}^{[n]}$ has $\mathrm{coVC}=0$, whereas its subfamily $\{\{i\}:i\in[n]\}$ of all singleton concepts has $\mathrm{coVC}=n$: the all-zero trace is missing and all of its one-coordinate neighbours occur. Thus passage to a subfamily can increase coVC.

p_monotonic.proof: A hollow star in a projection $(\mathcal H_{|T})_{|S}$ is exactly a hollow star in $\mathcal H_{|S}$ for $S\subseteq T$.  Since co-VC maximizes over coordinate restrictions, projecting first cannot increase it.

c_monotonic.proof: Let a conditioned fibre, obtained by fixing labels on a finite coordinate set $F$, contain a hollow star on disjoint coordinates $S$ with missing centre $t$. Combine $t$ with the fixed labels on $F$; this sample is inconsistent with the original class. For every $x\in S$, a hollow-star neighbour is realized by a concept in the fibre, so deleting the constraint at $x$ makes the combined sample consistent. A minimal inconsistent subsample therefore contains every coordinate of $S$. Its one-coordinate deletion witnesses form a hollow star of the original class of size at least $|S|$. Thus conditioning cannot increase coVC. If the conditioned class is empty its coVC is zero, so the conclusion is immediate.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
